name: Placental Site Trophoblastic Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and clinical diagnostic criteria for PSTT

criteria.description: Presence of intermediate trophoblastic cells infiltrating the myometrium with characteristic morphology
Serum human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels elevated but typically lower than in choriocarcinoma
Positive staining for human placental lactogen (hPL) and Mel-CAM (CD146) with negative or low beta-hCG staining
Abnormal uterine bleeding or amenorrhea following pregnancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of intermediate trophoblastic proliferation with supportive immunohistochemistry and clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical findings; imaging and serum markers assist but are not definitive alone.

imaging: Chest X-ray or CT revealing pulmonary metastases
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; diagnosis based on histopathology and immunohistochemistry
other: Histopathological identification of intermediate trophoblastic cells
Immunohistochemical positivity for hPL and Mel-CAM (CD146)

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing biphasic trophoblastic proliferation including cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast
Usually presents with nodular lesions in the uterus or cervix

redFlags: Persistent abnormal uterine bleeding unresponsive to treatment
Evidence of metastatic disease (e.g., pulmonary symptoms, neurological deficits)
references: Seckl MJ, Sebire NJ, Berkowitz RS. Gestational trophoblastic disease: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Ann Oncol. 2013.
Shih IM. Molecular and cellular biology of gestational trophoblastic disease. Best Pract Res Clin Obstet Gynaecol. 2003.
